artists.biography:
65daysofstatic (also known by the abbreviations 65dos, 65days, or simply 65) are an instrumental post-rock and math rock band from Sheffield, England comprising Paul Wolinski, Joe Shrewsbury, Rob Jones and Simon Wright. The band has released five studio albums: The Fall of Math, One Time for All Time, The Destruction of Small Ideas, We Were Exploding Anyway, and Silent Running.

Initially, the band interspersed heavy, progressive, guitar-driven instrumental sections with live drums and off-beat sampled drums akin to those of Aphex Twin, although since their second album they have developed their work to include keyboard parts.

The band has released five studio albums: The Fall of Math, One Time for All Time, The Destruction of Small Ideas, We Were Exploding Anyway, and Silent Running.

Initially, the band interspersed heavy, progressive, guitar-driven instrumental sections with live drums and off-beat sampled drums akin to those of Aphex Twin, although since their second album they have developed their work to include keyboard parts.

perplexity.description:
No Man's Sky: Music For An Infinite Universe is a 2016 soundtrack album by British electronic rock band 65daysofstatic, released on Laced Records. The album was composed specifically for the video game No Man's Sky, blending expansive electronic soundscapes with dynamic rock elements to evoke the game's themes of exploration, isolation, and cosmic wonder. The music features layered synths, driving rhythms, and atmospheric textures, creating an immersive auditory experience that mirrors the game's procedurally generated universe. Tracks such as "Monolith," "Supermoon," and "Escape Velocity" showcase the band's signature fusion of post-rock intensity and electronic experimentation.

This album marks 65daysofstatic's second major soundtrack release, following their earlier work on Silent Running (2011), and stands as a significant entry in their discography for its ambitious scope and integration with interactive media. While the band is best known for their studio albums like Wild Light and One Time for All Time, No Man's Sky: Music For An Infinite Universe demonstrates their ability to adapt their sound to a narrative and environmental context. The album received positive attention for its originality and emotional depth, with critics praising its contribution to the game's atmosphere and its success as a standalone listening experience.
